blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Conformal prediction provides set-valued predictions with distribution-free coverage guarantees, making it attractive for high-stakes image classification. However, split conformal prediction is data-inefficient, while full conformal prediction (FCP), despite its stronger statistical efficiency, is computationally prohibitive at scale because it requires candidate-specific model refits at test time. We address this limitation by leveraging zero-shot vision-language models (VLMs) to guide scalable FCP in large label spaces. We introduce Targeted Full Conformal Prediction (T-FCP), which uses a lightweight inductive conformal predictor to prune unlikely labels and applies FCP only to the remaining candidates, reducing computation while retaining the formal guarantee of the combined conformal procedure. We further propose Stabilized Online LDA (SO-LDA), an efficient VLM adaptation solver based on rank-one inverse-covariance updates. Across multiple benchmarks, including ImageNet, T-FCP enables practical full-conformal image classification with modest test-time overhead, yielding efficient prediction sets and more stable empirical coverage than split conformal alternatives. Code is available: T-FCP

blocks.en: The data-efficiency challenge. Despite the SCP being the most common procedure for image classification, it is also inherently data-inefficient, as only a fraction of the available data contributes to training and to the empirical quantile estimation. This limitation is nontrivial: the marginal coverage guarantee holds only in expectation over the calibration samples, introducing finite-sample variability (i.e., a beta-binomial distribution on α \alpha and N N Vovk (2012) ; Hulsman (2022) ; Marques and Paulo (2025) ) that may lead to noticeable deviations from the target coverage when N N is small. For instance, a user specifying α = 0.1 \alpha=0.1 may observe empirical coverage closer to 85 % 85\% instead of 90 % 90\% in practice.

blocks.en: Contributions. In this work, we aim to enable the construction of full conformal image classifiers at scale. Our main observation is that in a large label space, despite not being intrinsically ordered, many classes may be weakly related to each other, e.g., “husky” and “toaster”, while some groups of categories might be more similar, e.g., “husky”, “malamute”, “Samoyed”, or “Greater Swiss Mountain dog” ( real examples from ImageNet ). Therefore, if an initial proxy were available to guide the FCP procedure toward the most likely labels for a new test image, the total runtime could be significantly reduced. Hence, we propose exploiting the open-vocabulary capabilities of pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs), such as CLIP Radford et al. (2021) . These provide zero-shot class prototypes via text descriptions for the target label domain, which, despite not being specialized in the downstream task, serve as proxies in the model’s embedding space to discard non-similar categories that are not considered in the FCP procedure for each test image. Technically, our contributions are: • We formalize Targeted Full Conformal Prediction (T-FCP), a procedure that only requires running FCP on a subset of the label space ( B1 ), defined by an ICP procedure guided by zero-shot class prototypes with provable coverage guarantees without requiring splits on calibration data. • To address the cost of multiple model fits ( B2 ), we introduce SO-LDA, an online Linear Discriminant Analysis solver for VLM adaptation that performs stable incremental class-prototype updates together with rank-one inverse-covariance updates. SO-LDA achieves performance close to expensive gradient-based solvers while being orders of magnitude faster. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework enables full conformal procedures on large-scale datasets with a modest latency overhead (e.g., ∼ 30 ​ ms \sim 30\,\text{ms} /image for ImageNet), yielding efficient sets and more stable coverage distributions than split conformal procedures.

blocks.en: We formalize Targeted Full Conformal Prediction (T-FCP), a procedure that only requires running FCP on a subset of the label space ( B1 ), defined by an ICP procedure guided by zero-shot class prototypes with provable coverage guarantees without requiring splits on calibration data.
blocks.zh: 我们正式确定目标完全一致预测(T-FCP),这个程序只需要在标签空间(B1)的子集上运行FCP,该子集由国际比较方案程序确定,其指导标准为零镜头类原型,可证明的覆盖性保证,而不需要分解校准数据.

blocks.en: To address the cost of multiple model fits ( B2 ), we introduce SO-LDA, an online Linear Discriminant Analysis solver for VLM adaptation that performs stable incremental class-prototype updates together with rank-one inverse-covariance updates. SO-LDA achieves performance close to expensive gradient-based solvers while being orders of magnitude faster.
blocks.zh: 为了解决多重型号适合(B2)的成本问题,我们引入了SO-LDA,这是用于VLM适应的在线线性差异分析解析器,它进行稳定的递增类原型更新,同时进行一级反相变更新. SO-LDA实现性能接近于昂贵的梯度解析器,同时更快的达到数量级.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Full conformal prediction. Recent work on full conformal prediction has focused on reducing its computational burden, e.g., by limiting the candidate label space evaluated at test time. In regression, this has been achieved by exploiting the natural ordering of the response space, either through discretization Lei et al. (2013) ; Lei et al. (2018) or homotopy/continuation methods that track the solution path of the fitted model as the candidate response varies Lei et al. (2018) ; Lei (2019) ; Guha et al. (2023) ; Li (2024) . Classification problems, however, do not directly admit these strategies. Existing work for classification has instead focused on online classifiers with decoupled test-time updates, including exact permutation-invariant updates for kNN and SVMs Cherubin et al. (2021) , as well as inexact updates for gradient-based solvers via influence functions Martinez et al. (2023) .
blocks.zh: 完全一致的预测。 最近关于完全一致预测的工作侧重于减少其计算负担,例如限制在测试时评价的候选标签空间。 在回归过程中,通过利用反应空间的自然定序,通过光碟化Lei等人(2013年);Lei等人(2018年)或跟踪装配型号溶液路径的同位素/连续方法实现这一点,因为候选反应不同Lei等人(2018年);Lei (2019年);Guha等人(2023年);Li (2024年)。 然而,分类问题并不直接承认这些战略。 现有的分类工作则侧重于具有脱钩测试时间更新的在线分类器,包括kNN和SVMs Cherubin等人(2021年)的准确的演化-变量更新,以及通过影响函数Martinez等人(2023年)为梯度解析器提供的不准确更新.

blocks.en: Conformal prediction for image classification. Most neural-network-based image classification works follow SCP Einbinder et al. (2022) ; Stutz et al. (2022) ; Angelopoulos et al. (2020) ; Ding et al. (2023) ; Huang et al. (2024) ; Campos et al. (2025) ; Ding et al. (2026) , improving either training objectives for set efficiency Einbinder et al. (2022) ; Stutz et al. (2022) or nonconformity scores for adaptiveness, class-conditional coverage, and robustness Angelopoulos et al. (2020) ; Campos et al. (2025) ; Ding et al. (2023) ; Ding et al. (2026) . In contrast, calibration-data efficiency and empirical coverage variability have received less attention, as these methods typically rely on in-domain training data and separate calibration splits.
blocks.zh: 图像分类的正式预测. 多数基于神经网络的图像分类工作都遵循SCP Einbinder等人(2022年);Stutz等人(2022年);Angelopoulos等人(2020年);Ding等人(2023年);Huang等人(2024年);Campos等人(2025年);Ding等人(2026年),改进了设定效率的培训目标Einbinder等人(2022年);Stutz等人(2022年),或适应性、类覆盖率和强性Angelopoulos等人(2020年);Campos等人(2025年);Ding等人(2023年);Ding等人(2026年)。 相比之下,校准数据的效率和实证覆盖面的可变性受到的关注较少,因为这些方法通常依赖于域内培训数据和单独的校准分裂.

blocks.en: Conformal prediction for zero-shot models. Recent works have explored split conformal prediction for vision foundation models Fillioux et al. (2026) and, more specifically, vision-language models (VLMs) Silva-Rodríguez et al. (2025b) . Several methods improve VLM adaptation within conformal procedures using unsupervised transductive adaptation Silva-Rodríguez et al. (2025b) ; Silva-Rodríguez et al. (2025a) ; Bozorgtabar et al. (2026) . Closer to our work, Silva-Rodríguez and others (2025b) explored full conformal classifiers using closed-form linear solvers in the VLM embedding space. However, Silva-Rodríguez and others (2025b) focused on small-scale datasets ( C < 50 C<50 ). As we show later, their proposed kNN-style solver, SS-Text, does not scale well to large label spaces and fine-grained classification tasks.
blocks.zh: 零射线模型的正式预测. 最近的工作探索了视觉基础模型Fillioux 等人(2026年)的分裂结构预测,更具体地说,探索了视觉语言模型(VLMs)Silva-Rodríguez 等人(2025b). 一些方法利用未经监督的转录适应Silva-Rodríguez等人(2025b),Silva-Rodríguez等人(2025a),Bozorgtabar等人(2026),改进了在符合性程序范围内对VLM的适应。 更接近于我们的工作,Silva-Rodríguez等人(2025b)在VLM嵌入空间中,利用闭式线性解析器,探索了完全一致的分类器. 然而,Silva-Rodríguez等人(2025b)侧重于小规模数据集(C < 50 C < 50)。 正如我们后来所显示的那样,他们提出的kNN风格的解析器SS-Text没有很好地扩展到大的标签空间和精细的分类任务.

blocks.en: Combining conformal predictors. Related to our work are methods that combine or cascade multiple split conformal procedures Fisch et al. (2021) ; Timans et al. (2024) ; Sangalli et al. (2025) . For example, conformal cascades progressively prune candidate sets obtained with different nonconformity scores Fisch et al. (2021) . Other works derive combined coverage guarantees, either through multiplicative bounds under independence assumptions Timans et al. (2024) , or by allocating individual error rates using common corrections such as Bonferroni Timans et al. (2024) ; Sangalli et al. (2025) . These approaches have been used to achieve goals such as label-dependent guarantees for object detection Timans et al. (2024) and joint guarantees across multiple outputs Sangalli et al. (2025) .
blocks.zh: 结合一致预测器. 与我们的工作有关的是结合或连带多种分解调理程序Fisch等人(2021);Timans等人(2024);Sangalli等人(2025)。 例如,以不同的不合格分数Fisch等人(2021年)逐步获得的符合性级联。 其他作品通过独立假设Timans等人(2024年)下的多重界限,或者通过使用共同的更正(Bonferroni Timans等人(2024年);Sangalli等人(2025年)等来分配个人误差率,获得综合覆盖保障。 这些方法被用于实现各种目标,如对Timans等人(2024年)的检测进行依赖标签的保障,以及跨越多种产出的联合保障Sangalli等人(2025年)。

blocks.en: Second, we exploit the capabilities of zero-shot models to alleviate the second bottleneck in full conformal prediction ( B2 ): the computational cost of fitting the classifier for each extended dataset.

blocks.en: Transfer learning. Instead of training a deep network for each extended dataset, we leverage the rich embedding representation of pre-trained vision-language models, similarly to Silva-Rodríguez and others (2025b) . Given a dataset with labeled visual examples, and its corresponding embeddings, 𝒟 N = { ( 𝐯 i , y i ) } i = 1 N \mathcal{D}_{N}=\{(\mathbf{v}_{i},y_{i})\}_{i=1}^{N} , a common strategy is to learn task-specific linear class prototypes 𝐖 𝒟 N \mathbf{W}^{\mathcal{D}_{N}} , that replace its zero-shot counterpart in Eq. 7 to produce softmax class scores.

blocks.en: Online LDA. While several linear probe solvers have been proposed in the literature Gao et al. (2023) ; Silva-Rodríguez et al. (2024) ; Wang et al. (2024) , gradient-descent-based minimization of softmax cross-entropy is generally the best-performing solution Lin et al. (2023) ; Silva-Rodríguez et al. (2024) . However, its computational cost ( 𝒪 ⁡ ( T ​ N ​ F ​ C ) \mathcal{O}(TNFC) , with T T the number of iterations) makes it infeasible for full conformal prediction. blocks.en: Calibration sets. The corresponding test partition from each dataset is used in our conformal experiments to produce disjoint calibration and test subsets. Specifically, samples of size N = C × K N=C\times K , with K K the so-called number of shots in the transfer learning literature Zhou et al. (2022) ; Gao et al. (2023) ; Silva-Rodríguez et al. (2024) , are retrieved for calibration. By default, we set K = 16 K=16 , a standard data regime in transfer learning from VLMs Zhou et al. (2022) ; Gao et al. (2023) ; Silva-Rodríguez et al. (2024) , and present ablation studies with smaller sample sizes. Note that, in contrast to the standard literature on transfer learning from VLMs, which samples label-balanced adaptation sets, we follow the practice in conformal prediction Silva-Rodríguez et al. (2025b) ; Silva-Rodríguez et al. (2025a) that maintains the dataset’s label-marginal distribution in the calibration data to avoid breaking exchangeability assumptions. All experiments are repeated 50 times using different random seeds for sampling the calibration data.

blocks.en: Baselines. First, we compare our conformal procedure with standard ones in the literature: • Inductive conformal prediction (ICP): uses the whole calibration sample for quantile search, and computes the nonconformity score using the zero-shot scores (ZS) without adaptation. • Split conformal prediction (SCP): splits the calibration data into two equally-sized subsets, one for adaptation and the other for conformal quantile search. Since SCP is inductive, there is no computational restriction during the adaptation stage; therefore, we used standard softmax cross-entropy minimization via iterative gradient descent (GD). Training details are in Appendix E . • Full conformal prediction (FCP): performs the full conformal procedure over the whole label space. Adaptation is performed using our proposed SO-LDA solver. Second, we include ICP procedures that perform unsupervised transductive adaptation (ICP-T), recently proposed for VLMs Silva-Rodríguez et al. (2025b) ; Silva-Rodríguez et al. (2025a) ; Bozorgtabar et al. (2026) . Training details are in Appendix E .

blocks.en: 4.2 Main results
blocks.zh: 4.2 主要成果

blocks.en: Standard conformal procedures. Table 1 provides the results obtained with the different conformal procedures, and Figure 1 (a) illustrates the empirical coverage distribution for the main conformal alternatives. 1 In terms of coverage , it is worth noting that, despite all procedures achieving the target average coverage, SCP’s coverage deviation across samples is 20 % 20\% relatively larger than ICP’s, due to the data split. This is not the case for FCP procedures, which provide narrower coverage distributions, as in ICP. Notably, T-FCP achieves the largest proportion of experiments with valid coverage among these procedures: 81.8 % 81.8\% and 88.7 % 88.7\% for α = 0.10 \alpha=0.10 and α = 0.05 \alpha=0.05 , respectively. This is explained by the theoretically expected slightly over-coverage produced by the union-bound error rate design, i.e., α ICP \alpha_{\text{ICP}} , for early label pruning. 2 Regarding set efficiency , ICP produces the largest set sizes, since it does not benefit from transfer learning with labeled data. SCP and FCP provide similar mean set sizes. However, the median indicates that FCP produces set sizes that are ∼ 10 % \sim 10\% smaller (more efficient) than SCP, while its number of singletons (better on the discriminative aspect) is larger by a considerable margin. We explain these mixed observations in Figure 1 (b), showing that FCP using SO-LDA presents longer tails in the set size distribution, i.e., larger sets on uncertain inputs. This is explained by the design of the FCP, which inflates the conformity of each image-label candidate by training in the extended dataset, and the differences in optimization objectives between solvers. Finally, T-FCP provides slightly more conservative (larger) sets than FCP, with the advantage of enabling its real-time application on large-scale datasets, as discussed later. Still, T-FCP improves the median set size and singleton rate relative to SCP.

blocks.en: Computational efficiency. Figure 2 (a) showcases the latency scaling, in images per second, for full conformal procedures with the number of categories. Our experiments estimate that running the full conformal procedure using the iterative GD solver on ImageNet would require ∼ 500 ​ s \sim 500\,\text{s} per image, which is infeasible, as generally assumed in the literature. By using our SO-LDA solver, such latency is dramatically reduced to ∼ 0.33 ​ s \sim 0.33\,\text{s} , and is further decreased to ∼ 30 ​ ms \sim 30\,\text{ms} when pruning unlikely labels via our proposed T-FCP procedure. Regarding GPU usage, we parallelized the number of tested labels in the FCP procedure to 100 100 , which maintains, as depicted in Figure 2 (b), a top-up peak-GPU memory consumption of ∼ 16 ​ Gb \sim 16\,\text{Gb} on the largest dataset, i.e., ImageNet. However, as shown in Figure 2 (b), such a limit can be decreased without sacrificing much latency.

blocks.en: Label pruning stage. Figure 3 (a) provides a visualization of the pruning capabilities of the inductive stage of our T-FCP procedure across datasets. Figure 3 (a, left ) shows that most categories are discarded with small α ICP \alpha_{\text{ICP}} , specifically the elbow is found near 1 % 1\% of the allowed error rate. Therefore, most computational efficiency gains can be achieved without sacrificing much of the error-rate budget for the full conformal stage. Figure 3 (a, center ) shows a correlation between the zero-shot performance and the pruning capabilities; thus, T-FCP will be more computationally efficient the stronger the zero-shot model initially is. However, upon a closer look to Figure 3 (a, center and right ), large-scale datasets, such as SUN397 ( ) or ImageNet ( ), present larger pruning ratios than their zero-shot accuracy (nearly 60 − 70 % 60-70\% ) would imply. These results suggest that our T-FCP procedure is especially effective on the largest-scale datasets, where inter-class heterogeneities are greater and therefore categories with unrelated visual content are more easily pruned.

blocks.en: SO-LDA configuration and performance. Figure 4 (e) compares the discriminative performance of the different relevant linear solvers across increasing data regimes. First, it is worth noting that methods that rely solely on class centers, e.g., Simple-shot (SS) Wang and others (2019) ; Silva-Rodríguez and others (2025b) , despite their computational efficiency, fall short in performance compared to the best performing method, i.e., using iterative gradient-descent updates (GD), which makes them uncompetitive for full conformal procedures compared to SCP. Our proposed stabilized LDA solver with zero-shot guided feature centering in Eq. 16 consistently improves the performance of the learned prototypes compared to vanilla LDA Wang et al. (2024) . We attribute this behavior to the fact that visual examples within a category may be highly correlated in a specific visual domain, whereas textual information can improve the estimation of the main directions of dispersion in class distributions. Notably, SO-LDA reached performances closer to the expensive iterative GD solver, just ∼ 1.5 % \sim 1.5\% below. The constraint that learned prototypes remain close to their initial configurations in Eq. 17 helped stabilize performance gains in lower data regimes, as already observed in prior work on transfer learning from VLMs Khattak et al. (2023) ; Lin et al. (2023) ; Silva-Rodríguez et al. (2024) ; Silva-Rodríguez and others (2025a) .

blocks.en: Performance atop other VLMs. We evaluate the conformal procedures on additional backbones, including CLIP Radford et al. (2021) and MetaCLIP Xu et al. (2024) , in Figure 5 . The merits of T-FCP hold across all backbones, providing consistently more concentrated empirical coverage distributions than SCP, with variances ∼ 30 % \sim 30\% smaller, while maintaining valid coverage. Moreover, predictive accuracy and set efficiency are consistently improved, especially compared to ICP. This is even the case for larger-scale backbones, e.g., MetaCLIP ViT-L/14, for which the median set size is reduced by 31 % 31\% , without sacrificing finite-sample coverage stability. Despite the strong reliance of T-FCP and our SO-LDA solver on zero-shot prototypes, performance remains robust also in smaller backbones, e.g., ViT-B/32.

blocks.en: 5 Discussion
blocks.zh: 5 讨论情况

blocks.en: We presented T-FCP and SO-LDA, enabling full conformal prediction on large-scale image datasets by leveraging zero-shot VLMs. Our experiments highlight that data-efficient procedures yield more stable empirical coverage than split-based alternatives and underscore the importance of data efficiency in conformal image classification.
blocks.zh: 我们介绍了T-FCP和SO-LDA,通过利用零射VLM,使得能够对大型图像数据集进行全面的一致预测。 我们的实验强调,数据效率高的程序比基于分法的替代品更能提供稳定的实证覆盖,并强调数据效率在符合图象分类中的重要性。

blocks.en: Limitations. The proposed linear solver is still less performant than iterative gradient-based methods. Although this gap is partially compensated for in FCP by fitting on each candidate-augmented dataset, we cannot guarantee that the resulting prediction sets will always be more efficient than those from SCP, which can use more expensive solvers during its adaptation stage. A further limitation is that our main SO-LDA implementation uses diagonal loading to stabilize the precision matrix, thereby approximating recomputing a fully regularized LDA estimator for each augmented dataset. Therefore, although T-FCP offers theoretically valid coverage, the same is not true when it is combined with our SO-LDA solver. In practice, ablations in Appendix C show negligible differences against exact implementations. Finally, the coverage guarantee of T-FCP is based on an additive union-bound allocation across the pruning and full-conformal stages. Consequently, the resulting sets may be slightly more conservative than FCP’s. Hence, FCP may be preferred for smaller-scale tasks, e.g., those involving tens or a few hundred classes, especially when coupled with our online LDA solver.
blocks.zh: 限制。 拟议线性解析器的性能仍然不如基于迭代梯度的方法. 虽然在FCP中通过安装每个候选数据集来部分弥补这一缺口,但我们不能保证由此产生的预测集总是比SCP的预测集更有效,SCP在适应阶段可以使用更昂贵的解析器. 另一个限制因素是,我们SO-LDA的主要实施使用对角加载来稳定精度矩阵,从而接近于为每个扩充数据集重新计算一个完全规范化的LDA估计器。 因此,虽然T-FCP提供理论上有效的覆盖,但当它与我们的SO-LDA解析器结合时,情况并非如此. 在实践中,附录C中的浮提表明,与具体执行的差别微不足道。 最后,T-FCP的覆盖保障是基于在运行阶段和正式阶段的附加工会分配。 因此,所产生的套装可能略高于燃料加工中心。 因此,对于规模较小的任务,例如涉及几十个班级或几百个班级的任务,尤其是与我们的在线LDA解析器结合时,FCP可能更受青睐.

blocks.en: Appendix A Broader Impacts
blocks.zh: 附录A 更广泛的影响

blocks.en: Broader impacts. Conformal prediction is often motivated by providing theoretical guarantees in high-stakes deployment. However, it should be interpreted with care. Marginal coverage does not imply conditional or subgroup coverage, and guarantees need not hold under distribution shift. Moreover, finite-sample empirical coverage can fall below the nominal level in a real-world deployment, especially with data-inefficient pipelines. In this work, we directly address the latter use case, enabling more stable conformal image classifiers via full conformal prediction. We do not anticipate negative societal impacts from our work beyond those of standard conformal prediction, and we identify no domain-specific risks requiring special attention.
blocks.zh: 更大的影响。 在高吸量部署中,提供理论保障常常是促成非正式预测的。 然而,应谨慎解释。 边际保险并不意味着有条件的或次级保险,保证不必在分配的转变中坚持。 此外,在现实世界的部署中,有限的抽样经验覆盖可能低于名义水平,特别是数据效率低下的管道。 在这项工作中,我们直接处理后者的使用情况,通过完全一致的预测,使图像分类更加稳定。 我们预计我们的工作不会产生超出标准一致性预测的负面社会影响,我们发现没有具体领域的风险需要特别关注。

blocks.en: Appendix C Stability of SO-LDA
blocks.zh: 附录C SO-LDA的稳定

blocks.en: In this section, we further analyze SO-LDA, particularly the implications of the mild asymmetry introduced by the diagonal covariance matrix regularization used in the main implementation, whose diagonal is estimated only from calibration data to enable efficient rank-one updates. We compare such a solution with different configurations: • Ridge : the regularization is imposed via a fixed identity loading, 𝐒 ( N ) reg = 𝐒 ( N ) + λ RIDGE ​ 𝐈 \mathbf{S}^{\mathrm{reg}}_{(N)}=\mathbf{S}_{(N)}+\lambda_{\mathrm{RIDGE}}\mathbf{I} , which is compatible with permutation-invariant rank-one updates under fixed regularization. • Non-online : for each candidate sample-label pair, it recomputes the class means and the covariance matrix from the full augmented dataset, then directly inverts the regularized covariance matrix. This solver increases the per-label computational cost to 𝒪 ⁡ ( N ​ F 2 + F 3 ) \mathcal{O}(NF^{2}+F^{3}) . • Unstable : does not use zero-shot prototypes for the residuals estimation as in Eq. 16 . Hence, the centered features are calculated asymmetrically between calibration and test data. Comparative performance on different data regimes is presented in Table 2 . The results suggest that the dominant source of instability is the asymmetric centering of the residuals used for covariance estimation, with the Unstable configuration yielding the largest marginal coverage gap and lower ratio of valid occurrences. The fixed- Ridge configuration is the cleanest variant with respect to symmetric online updates. However, its discriminative performance is lower than that of our diagonal regularization in SO-LDA. Moreover, both exhibit a similar coverage distribution, suggesting that the asymmetry introduced by our implementation choice is negligible. Also, the performance levels achieved by SO-LDA are similar to those obtained with more expensive, exact Non-online updates.

blocks.en: Gradient-descent linear probe (GD). We followed training details similar to [ 47 ] , which remain fixed for all datasets. The learned class weights are initialized with zero-shot prototypes. Full-batch gradient descent is performed for 300 300 iterations, minimizing cross-entropy. SGD is used as the optimizer with momentum 0.9 0.9 . A cosine-annealing scheduler with a base learning rate of 0.1 0.1 is applied to ensure a small step size and proper convergence.

blocks.en: It is worth noting that adaptive scores such as APS/RAPS require ranking or sorting over the label space. This adds non-negligible cost inside the candidate-wise FCP loop, which conflicts with our scalability focus. For example, for ImageNet, T-FCP [ α ICP = 0.5 % , α FCP = 9.5 % \alpha_{\text{ICP}}=0.5\%,\ \alpha_{\text{FCP}}=9.5\% ] using LAC has a latency of nearly 30 ms/image, and it increases to nearly 220 ms/image using APS, which makes it currently less appealing to use for the largest-scale datasets for T-FCP and unfeasible for the more expensive vanilla FCP.
blocks.zh: 值得注意的是,APS/RAPS等适应性分数需要对标签空间进行排名或排序. 这在候选的FCP环内增加了不可忽略的成本,这与我们的可扩展性重点相冲突. 例如,对于ImageNet,T-FCP [α CP = 0.5%,α FCP = 9.5%\alpha_{\text{ICP}}= 0.5\%,\ alpha_{\text{FCP}}=9.5\%] 使用LAC的耐久度为近30ms/image,使用APS的耐久度增加到近220ms/image,这使得目前对T-FCP使用最大的数据集的吸引力降低,对更昂贵的香草FCP则无法使用.

blocks.en: F.4 Extension to unimodal models
blocks.zh: F.4 推广到单式模式

blocks.en: The T-FCP construction is model-agnostic in principle: any valid low-cost conformal predictor could be used as the pruning stage, and any valid or efficient FCP scoring rule could be used as the second stage. Beyond VLMs, T-FCP can therefore be explored for unimodal models as long as an initial pruning proxy exists, e.g., a pretrained classifier over the target label space.
blocks.zh: T-FCP构造原则上是模型-不可知的:任何有效的低成本向导预测器都可以作为普鲁士阶段,任何有效或高效的FCP评分规则都可以作为第二阶段. 因此,在VLMs之外,只要存在一个初始的推算代理,例如,在目标标签空间上预加训练的分类器,T-FCP就可以被探索单式模型.

blocks.en: To test this, we next transfer a standard ResNet-50 model pretrained on ImageNet to ImageNet-V2 (accuracy 69.1%), since the two datasets share the same label space.
